title: One-time codes are keyed by the session signer and refused without a secret in production
objective: Every email-verification and password-reset one-time code is HMAC'd with the same key the session signer resolves: the configured ALGORIK_SESSION_SECRET (or its _FILE), refused when shorter than 32 characters, refused outright when NODE_ENV is production and none is configured, and a per-process random key in development. No string literal keys any HMAC in frontend/portal/src/lib/server.
why: codeHash() (identity.ts:104-110) resolves its key as `configuredSessionSecret() ?? "algorik-development"`. configuredSessionSecret() returns null whenever the mounted secret is absent or empty, and the production refusal lives only in session.ts's signingKey() (session.ts:144-162), which codeHash never calls. A production deployment whose secret file failed to mount would therefore key every stored code hash with a literal anyone can read in this repository instead of refusing - the fail-open shape CLAUDE.md principle 3 forbids, in the file family whose own comment records that the cookie signer already fell back to a development key once. What that key protects is narrower than the title suggests, and this packet claims only that: issueCode and redeemCode are reached only on the development provider (developmentProviderActive(), identity.ts:142), whose store (identity.json, identity-store.ts:69) holds each code as its HMAC; with the key public, anyone who can read the store recovers a six-digit code offline in at most 10^6 HMACs. The key is NOT what protects the live reset flow: on a production build the development provider returns the plaintext code (identity.ts:476, and :261/:282/:456 for verification) and the routes put it in the HTTP response for any registered email (api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:27-28, sign-up/route.ts:54, resend-verification/route.ts:19-20); infrastructure/gitops/envs/dev/portal.yaml:96-107 deploys exactly that shape (no ALGORIK_IDENTITY_PROJECT_ID, `next start`). That exposure is FIX-16's, latent today (gitops_iap_members = [] in environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:648 and ADR 0093 suspends the reconciler), and FIX-01 does not close it. scripts/deploy-frontends.sh:265 sets ALGORIK_IDENTITY_PROJECT_ID and is unaffected by either. Source: docs/reports/tech-debt/frontend.json, the row at index 5 (class B-refactor, 'identity.ts's one-time-code HMAC key silently falls back to a hardcoded literal'). No requirement in docs/blueprint/requirements states this property - SEC-017 is IAP reachability and is FIX-02's - so `requirements` is empty rather than borrowed. Confirmed at 42fb3c07: identity.ts:108 is the literal fallback; no spec under frontend/portal/tests names codeHash or the literal.

title: A grant's drawdown limit fires because the cell books realised loss from its fills

title: No production build of the portal puts a one-time code in an HTTP response
deferred_until: FIX-01 merges (wave 1): identity.ts and tests/one-time-code-key.spec.ts are its files
objective: On a production build (NODE_ENV=production, which every `next start` is), no response from /api/auth/sign-up, /api/auth/forgot-password or /api/auth/resend-verification carries a one-time code, and no rendered page shows one: one helper in identity.ts decides whether a code may enter a response and answers no on every production build, the three routes go through it and nothing else, forgot-password's answer stays identical for a registered and an unregistered address, and no environment variable, header or config can re-admit a code. In `next dev` behaviour is unchanged. Proven by a Playwright spec against a production-mode server on the development provider.
why: Found in review of FIX-01, not in the numbered defect list. On the development provider (no ALGORIK_IDENTITY_PROJECT_ID) forgotPassword returns the plaintext reset code (identity.ts:476), signUp and resendVerification the verification code (:282, :456), and the routes put it in the HTTP response for any registered email (forgot-password/route.ts:27-28, sign-up/route.ts:54, resend-verification/route.ts:19-20). Nothing checks the build: identity.ts's own header (:46-54) says devCode 'is never populated once a real provider is configured', which is a statement about the provider, not about production. infrastructure/gitops/envs/dev/portal.yaml:96-107 deploys the portal on the development provider under `next start`, so on that deployment anyone who reaches the route can take over any account by requesting its reset code - the HMAC key FIX-01 fixes does not enter into it. Latent today: gitops_iap_members = [] (environments/dev/terraform.tfvars:648) and ADR 0093 suspends the reconciler; scripts/deploy-frontends.sh:265 sets ALGORIK_IDENTITY_PROJECT_ID and is unaffected. The test suite pins the exposure: auth.spec.ts:74-80 runs against `next start` (playwright.config.ts:103-109, :228-249) and asserts the development code IS surfaced on screen. Tier T4: authentication and credentials (ADR 0098 §2). Confirmed at 42fb3c07.
